review_candidates.title: Head of manufacturing
review_candidates.description: Join a unique greenfield project Make a lasting impact on the company's expansion across the Americas. About Our Client Leading global company specializing in motorcycle manufacturing. Job Description As Head of Manufacturing you will be responsible for leading the development, start-up, and overall operation of a new motorcycle OEM manufacturing facility in Mexico. You will oversee the execution of the greenfield project, the development of the plant's organizational structure, the implementation of operational processes, production readiness, and the stabilization of operations. You will also have full responsibility for the plant's P&L, ensuring the achievement of safety, quality, cost, delivery, productivity, and profitability targets. You will directly lead the Production, Quality, Supply Chain, Maintenance, and Finance functions, while also overseeing Assembly, Logistics, Warehousing, Manufacturing Engineering, and Continuous Improvement. Your responsibilities will cover the entire operational flow, from the receipt of materials and components through manufacturing, distribution, and delivery of finished products to the dealer network. The Successful Applicant A Successful Head Of Manufacturing Should Have Between 10 and 15 years of experience in the automotive industry, with direct experience working for an automotive OEM. At least seven years of experience in leadership positions such as Plant Manager, Plant Director, Operations Manager, Manufacturing Manager, Production Manager, or an equivalent role. Experience leading an end-to-end manufacturing operation, with responsibility for Production, Quality, Maintenance, Engineering, Supply Chain, Logistics, and support functions. Demonstrated experience in greenfield projects, plant start-ups, production line installation, new product launches, or industrial ramp-up processes. Strong knowledge of high-volume manufacturing, vehicle assembly, production planning, inventory management, and material flow. Direct experience managing P&L, operating budgets, CAPEX, conversion costs, working capital, and plant profitability. Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, productivity enhancement, structured problem-solving, and process standardization. Experience in supplier development, evaluation, and performance management, preferably with exposure to component localization projects. Advanced English proficiency, required to interact with, present results to, and report to international teams and senior leaders. Hands-on leadership style, strong people orientation, effective communication, influencing skills, strategic thinking, operational discipline, integrity, and the ability to build teams and processes from the ground up. What's on Offer Competitive salary and benefits package Contact: Luis Galindo Quote job ref: JN-092026-7115029

review_candidates.title: HR Technology Analyst
review_candidates.description: Position Overview Under the general direction of the Chief People Officer, the HR Technology Analyst serves as an experienced functional and analytical resource for Human Resources technology, data, reporting, and process improvement. The role independently evaluates complex business needs, translates requirements into scalable system and reporting solutions, safeguards data quality, and provides actionable workforce insights that support organizational goals. The position leads assigned initiatives, exercises sound judgment in resolving complex issues, and partners with Human Resources, Information Technology, Finance, business leaders, and vendors to improve HR systems and operations. Scope Of Role & Responsibilities Act as a subject-matter resource for assigned HRIS modules, reporting tools, interfaces, and related HR technology; independently analyze complex issues, determine root causes, and recommend practical solutions. Partner with HR functional leaders and business stakeholders to define workforce metrics, reporting standards, and data requirements aligned with operational and strategic priorities. Design, develop, validate, and maintain scalable dashboards, reports, and queries covering recruitment, onboarding, employee movement, labor relations, compensation, attendance, turnover, workforce demographics, and other key measures. Monitor HR data quality, perform complex audits and reconciliations, investigate discrepancies across systems, and establish controls that improve accuracy, completeness, consistency, and timeliness. Evaluate data sources, collection methods, benchmarks, and technical options; recommend solutions that improve operational efficiency, automation, reporting reliability, and the employee or manager experience. Prepare executive-ready workforce analyses, dashboards, presentations, and decision-support materials for the Chief People Officer, Executive Team, and other stakeholders. Manage recurring and ad hoc compensation survey submissions, data updates, reconciliations, and reporting in partnership with Compensation and other stakeholders. Collect, validate, and report Labor Relations data while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and access controls. Create and maintain organizational charts, position-management reports, and related workforce-structure documentation. Develop and maintain business-process documentation, data definitions, report inventories, and standard operating procedures. Provide guidance and technical support to HR users; explain complex system or data concepts clearly, identify training needs, and promote consistent use of HR technology and reporting standards. Coordinate with Information Technology, vendors, and functional owners on integrations, file feeds, issue resolution, release planning, and service delivery; escalate material risks appropriately. Maintain trusted client partnerships through regular communication, consultative problem-solving, and effective representation of Human Resources. May provide project guidance, peer review, or knowledge transfer to analysts and other team members without direct supervisory responsibility. Perform other related duties and projects as assigned. Required Education, Training & Professional Experience Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Information Technology, Human Resources, Business Administration, Data Analytics, or a related field; or a satisfactory equivalent combination of education, training, and experience. Master’s Degree preferred. Four (4) years of progressively responsible experience in HRIS, HR business systems, workforce analytics, data analysis, or a closely related area, including experience independently supporting complex business requirements and system or reporting initiatives. Experience with at least one commercial HRIS platform and a strong understanding of HRIS concepts, system configuration, functional analysis, system design, testing, data structures, and reporting. Demonstrated experience creating complex reports, dashboards, queries, and data analyses for business and executive audiences. Working knowledge of HR operations, policies, processes, data privacy, confidentiality, and access-control principles. Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Excel and proficiency with Microsoft Office applications; experience with data-visualization, reporting, query, or business-intelligence tools is strongly preferred. Preferred experience supporting HRIS implementations, upgrades, integrations, workflow automation, vendor-led enhancements, audit controls, position management, or organizational reporting. Preferred experience developing requirements, test plans, user documentation, training materials, or standard operating procedures. Required Licensure And/or Certification SHRM Certified Professional (SHRM-CP), SHRM Senior Certified Professional (SHRM-SCP), HRIP, or a relevant HR technology or analytics certification is preferred. Professional Competencies Integrity and Trust Customer Focus Functional and Technical Expertise Written and Oral Communication Independent Judgment and Decision-Making Analytical Thinking and Complex Problem-Solving Project Coordination and Execution Cross-Functional Collaboration and Influence Organization, Documentation, and Attention to Detail Discretion and Protection of Confidential Information #MHP50
